title: Mouse without Borders: Disable Easy Mouse when an application is running in full screen - setting is triggered by windowless desktop
author: forslu

judgment.rationale: The report has a deterministic desktop reproduction and two independent workaround paths: disabling the fullscreen option or excluding explorer.exe/VLC. This supports a focused fix for false fullscreen classification.
evidence: With all windows minimized, Easy Mouse stops crossing PCs when Disable Easy Mouse for fullscreen applications is enabled.
Disabling the option avoids the problem.
Adding explorer.exe to ignored fullscreen applications fixes the desktop case.
A user reports non-fullscreen VLC also triggering the condition and being fixed by exclusion.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue a Mouse Without Borders fullscreen-detection design that uses actual foreground presentation state rather than broad process/window presence.

fix_assessment.rationale: The false-positive boundary is clear, but current detection code was not inspected during this lightweight pass.

proposed_fixes.title: Restrict Mouse Without Borders fullscreen suppression to the actual foreground fullscreen window
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Easy Mouse fullscreen check treats the desktop shell or a non-fullscreen VLC window as a blocking fullscreen application, so edge switching is disabled on false positives.
plan: Trace the current fullscreen predicate and the window/process chosen when the desktop or VLC is active.
Require a visible foreground presentation that actually covers the relevant monitor before disabling Easy Mouse.
Keep the ignored-app list as an override and add regression cases for explorer.exe, windowed VLC, and true fullscreen apps.
verification: Show the desktop and cross the configured edge with fullscreen suppression enabled.
Repeat with windowed VLC and with a genuinely fullscreen application.

confidence.rationale: The false-positive behavior and workarounds are repeatable, but the exact window-selection predicate has not been inspected.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders falsely disables Easy Mouse on the desktop or with non-fullscreen-capable applications such as VLC.
known_information: The option is specifically Disable Easy Mouse when an application is running in full screen.
The Windows desktop can trigger it.
The ignore list is an effective workaround.
inferences: Fullscreen detection is likely considering an inappropriate shell or application window, but the exact predicate is unknown.
issue_context.analysis: The canonical issue is ready for code-level detection review and regression tests using explorer.exe and VLC.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the current public issue body, labels, assignees, and up to the latest 20 public comments returned by GitHub.
Kept the existing dashboard read-only; no dashboard files were modified or published.

actions.label: Approve restrict mouse without borders fullscreen suppression to the actual foreground fullscreen window
actions.note: Approve/start the fork-side design workflow from this public-evidence fix plan. No upstream write occurs from this action.

actions.label: Reproduce Mouse without Borders: Disable Easy Mouse when an application is running in full screen - setting is triggered by windowless desktop
actions.note: Maintainer-side reproduction reduces the recorded implementation uncertainty without asking the reporter to perform code investigation.

prerequisites: Easy Mouse and Disable Easy Mouse when an application is running in full screen enabled.
steps: Move the pointer across the configured edge.
Add explorer.exe to ignored fullscreen applications and repeat.
Repeat with VLC windowed and fullscreen.
reproduce.expected_result: Desktop and windowed apps allow crossing; only a true fullscreen app blocks it.
reproduce.observed_result: The desktop or windowed VLC can block crossing until excluded.
